notes:
Account snapshot: GlobalCrest is a large European online travel operator exploring multilingual contact center automation across EU/US/APAC markets. Primary driver: improve agent productivity on high-volume ticket days, reduce handle time, and offer localized tone per market. They care about translation quality + locale-aware tone (not literal translation).

Key requirements (summary):
- Workloads: real-time agent assist (low-latency suggestions), post-contact ticket summarization, out-of-band tool-calling (CRM updates, refund workflows).
- Latency: target 200-500ms per suggestion for short agent messages; end-to-end < 1s for ticket categorization.
- Throughput: steady-state 350-450 concurrent agents; burst capacity up to ~2,000 concurrent during peak travel disruptions.
- Cost sensitivity: willing to commit for Dedicated capacity if unit economics beat hosted. Wants clear batching/quantization suggestions to justify Dedicated.
- Model preferences: open models with quantized variants; fallback policy to smaller models for non-critical tasks. Explore Redwood Optimize for quantization profiles.
- Routing: regional routing by user locale with EU-only residency for EU customers; language-specific fallback to English if localized model unavailable.
- Security: enterprise SSO/SAML, KMS integration for key management, audit logs for compliance team, retention controls for EU data residency.

CRM-style excerpts from interactions:
- "Tone matters more in LATAM and APAC — must localize, not just translate" — Head of CX (call 2026-02-15).
- Demo feedback: agent assist suggestions reduced average typing time in pilot by ~12% (internal pilot notes).
- Security flagged: need legal sign-off on 3rd-party model telemetry; asked for detailed data-flow diagram (Drive: security-faq).

POC details and timeline: see timeline field for event list. Primary POC uses Dedicated pool in EU w/ private control plane; stress test scheduled 2026-02-01 through 2026-02-21. Redwood engineer embedded for first week to tune batching and KV cache settings.

Quotes/phrases to help AE notes: "If you can show consistent 2k spike handling with our tone rules, we can move to procurement."

use_case_summary: Multilingual contact center automation: combine low-latency agent assist with automated post-call summarization and safe tool-calling. Emphasis on localized tone and region-aware routing. Reliability during high-traffic travel disruptions is critical.
technical_requirements: Need ability to pin model versions per region, automated fallback to quantized variants when load high, KV/prefix caching for repeat queries, per-route latency SLOs, regional routing (EU-only for EU customer data).
po_c_success_metrics: Latency p50/p95 targets, summarization ROUGE/BLEU style quality thresholds per locale, agent productivity uplift %, and demonstration of handling 2k concurrent spikes with graceful degradation to smaller models.
recent_risks: Legal may require on-prem deployment for certain EU markets; this would push cost and extend timeline. Procurement is sensitive to capital vs. commit-based pricing.
